newsitem.title: USA: Tyson profits plunge despite record revenues.
newsitem.headline: Tyson profits plunge despite record revenues.

text.p: Tyson Foods Inc., the world's largest producer of chicken and poultry-based food products, Monday reported a sharp drop in fourth-quarter profits as high grain costs ate into record revenues.
Net income plunged to $14.6 million, or 10 cents a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 28 from $58.8 million, or 40 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales rose 14.3 percent to $1.69 billion from $1.48 billion, with poultry sales up 16.6 percent. Overall unit volume grew 9.9 percent, with poultry unit volume up 12.9 percent.
For the fiscal year, profits slid to $86.9 million, or 60 cents a share, from $219.2 million, or $1.51 a share, in the prior year. Sales rose to $6.5 billion from $5.5 billion.
"People are still eating chicken, but grain costs were the highest in recorded history this year," a Tyson spokeswoman said.
Tyson said it expects "marked improvements" in its earnings for 1997 beginning in the second quarter.

The projections are based on recent estimates by the U.S. Department of Agriculture and private forecasters that the 1996 feed grain and soybean crop will be "significantly larger" than late summer forecasts, Tyson Chairman and Chief Executive Leland Tollett said in a statement.
"As a result, we can expect much more moderate and stable feed prices for fiscal year 1997, with marked improvements in earnings beginning in the second quarter," Tollett said.
He added that demand for Tyson's products is strong, market conditions are stable and the company is "poised to take advantage of a business environment that continues to improve."
Tyson's stock rose $2.625 to $31 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
